c-ai-cubes.label: Cubes of big numbers
c-ai-cubes.summary: Add and subtract cubes of two-digit numbers without a calculator: last digit first, then a rough size.

c-ai-reciprocal.label: x + 1/x and its powers
c-ai-reciprocal.summary: One value of x + 1/x unlocks x² + 1/x² and x³ + 1/x³ through two small identities.

q-ai-cubes.label: Sum and difference of big cubes
q-ai-cubes.summary: Cubes of numbers like 32, 19 and 38 added, subtracted and adjusted.

q-ai-reciprocal.label: Value of x + 1/x
q-ai-reciprocal.summary: x is given (often a surd); find x + 1/x or a power of it.

formulas.text: Last digit of a cube: digits 0 to 9 give 0, 1, 8, 7, 4, 5, 6, 3, 2, 9
formulas.note: Only 2↔8 and 3↔7 swap; the rest repeat. Use it to kill options in seconds.

formulas.text: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)     a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)
formulas.note: Use when the numbers are related (a + b is round).

formulas.text: If a + b + c = 0 then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc
formulas.note: Check this first: it turns three big cubes into one product.
When x² is a whole number (x = √11) the top is a whole number at once.

q-ai-cubes.cue: Cubes of two-digit numbers joined by plus and minus, maybe with a small number added at the end.
q-ai-cubes.standard: Cube each number (square it, then multiply), add and subtract in order, then add the small number.
q-ai-cubes.fast: Find the last digit of the answer from the last digits of the cubes (2→8, 9→9, 8→2 here). Then rough-size each cube to settle the sign and the magnitude.
q-ai-cubes.eliminate: Work out the last digit of the true answer and strike every option that ends differently. In the PYQ here three of the four options end in 0.
traps: A sign slip when subtracting the biggest cube: the answer is negative.
Forgetting the small number at the end (+312).
variations: Three cubes with a + b + c = 0, so the sum is 3abc.
(a³ + b³) ÷ (a² − ab + b²), which is just a + b.

q-ai-reciprocal.cue: x is a surd or a simple number and the question asks for x + 1/x (or x² + 1/x²).
q-ai-reciprocal.standard: Write 1/x, rationalise it, add to x. Or use (x² + 1) ÷ x.
q-ai-reciprocal.fast: If x = √n then x² = n, so x + 1/x = (n + 1)/√n. Multiply top and bottom by √n to get (n + 1)√n / n.
q-ai-reciprocal.eliminate: Estimate x + 1/x (3.32 + 0.30 ≈ 3.62 for x = √11) and test each option numerically.
traps: Using x² + 2 instead of x² + 1 on top.
Forgetting to rationalise and picking an option with a different form.

pyqs.trick: Last digits: 2³ ends in 8, 9³ in 9, 8³ in 2, so the answer ends in 8 + 9 − 2 + 2 = 17 → 7. Only −14933 ends in 7 (−14933 = −14940 + 7); the other three all end in 0.

a.note: The true value ends in 7 (last digits 8 + 9 − 2 + 2 = 17), but -38520 ends in 0.

b.note: The true value ends in 7 (last digits 8 + 9 − 2 + 2 = 17), but -26840 ends in 0.

d.note: The true value ends in 7 (last digits 8 + 9 − 2 + 2 = 17), but -52100 ends in 0.

pyqs.text: If x = √11, find the value of x + 1/x.
pyqs.trick: (x² + 1)/x = 12/√11: the 12 is 11 + 1. Only option (a) has 12 on top and 11 underneath.
